This is a case of acute, severe, symptomatic hypoosmolar hyponatremia (Na 122 mEq/L, serum osmolality 258 mOsm/kg). The key diagnostic task is distinguishing among causes of euvolemic hypoosmolar hyponatremia. The patient is clinically euvolemic (no edema, orthostasis, or signs of volume depletion or overload), and thyroid function is normal (TSH 1.42), making primary hypothyroidism unlikely.
